evals.prompt: What queries is https://www.example.com/pricing getting in Google? Pull the last 3 months from Search Console for the Domain property example.com and give me a CSV.
evals.expected_output: Uses the property id sc-domain:example.com, an ISO date range covering the last 3 full months, an equals page filter on the exact URL, pages through results if a call returns exactly rowLimit rows, and saves a CSV with page, query, clicks, impressions, ctr (percent) and position. States that anonymised long-tail queries mean totals won't reconcile.
expectations: Uses 'sc-domain:example.com' as the property id, not the bare domain or a URL
Dates are passed in ISO YYYY-MM-DD format
Filters on the page dimension with operator equals and the exact URL
Output columns are page, query, clicks, impressions, ctr, position with CTR as a percentage
Mentions that Search Console anonymises rare queries so query totals won't match page totals
Never prints or writes the client secret, refresh token, access token or Authorization header

evals.prompt: Pull Search Console queries for every page under /blog/ on https://www.example.org/ (it's a URL-prefix property) for January to March 2026, including the last few days of data.
evals.expected_output: Uses the URL-prefix property id with trailing slash, pageOperator contains with /blog/, dataState all, dates 2026-01-01 to 2026-03-31, pages with startRow until a call returns fewer than rowLimit rows, and notes that the freshest days are not final and will change.
expectations: Uses 'https://www.example.org/' (full URL with trailing slash) as the property id
Uses the contains operator with the /blog/ path instead of listing URLs by hand
Sets dataState to all and warns that the last 2-3 days are not finalised
Pages through results with startRow when a call returns exactly rowLimit rows
Records the property, date range, match mode and dataState with the output

evals.prompt: Here are 12 URLs from blog.example.com. Get the GSC queries for each one for the last 90 days. I haven't set anything up for the Search Console API yet.
evals.expected_output: Checks for a Search Console connector or export first; since API credentials are missing, walks the user through the one-time OAuth setup (enable the Search Console API, Desktop OAuth client, refresh token for webmasters.readonly via the OAuth Playground) and has the user store the credentials themselves; then batches all 12 URLs, spacing calls, recording per-page row counts and listing zero-row pages with likely causes.
expectations: Offers the user's own Search Console connector or export as the first option
Explains the one-time setup: enable Google Search Console API, Desktop app OAuth client, refresh token with the webmasters.readonly scope
Has the user enter the credentials (environment variables or browser storage) rather than asking them to paste secrets into the chat
Batches the 12 URLs in one run and reports a row count or error per URL
Lists any zero-row URLs with likely causes such as URL variant mismatch, wrong property or no impressions
